newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: New ZCCM owners will inherit $580 mln debt.
newsitem.headline: New ZCCM owners will inherit $580 mln debt.

text.p: The new owners of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM), due to be privatised soon, will inherit the company's debts of around $580 million, the Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Friday.
"The company has long-term debts totalling 437 billion kwacha ($338.5 million) and short-term debts totalling 337 billion kwacha," a ZPA official said.
"The debts will be allocated to the various investors during privatisation negotiations," the official added.

Companies bidding for ZCCM assets, to be sold under 10 packages, include an Avmin-led consortium, Phelps Dodge Corp, Noranda Inc, Commonwealth Development Corp, Straits Resources Ltd and the Binani Group.
Bids for the company's assets were opened on February 28 and the government expects to conclude negotiations with successful bidders by the end of the year.
